document.title: Central Asian Reaction to Taliban's Takeover of Kabul (Mori Document 1161400)
document.authors: CIA, Office of Russian and Eurasian Analysis
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban Biography: The Structure and Leadership of the Taliban 1996-2002
document.note: [Secret] Assessment two weeks after the Taliban takeover of Kabul of Central Asian reaction. Only Pakistan recognizes the Taliban; neighbors are alarmed and fear instability, but have not decided on collective efforts to arm Taliban opponents. Identifies key Taliban figures including Mullah Omar. Excised.

events.description: Taliban capture Kabul
Emergency CIS Summit in Almaty on Afghan crisis; four Central Asian leaders (excluding Niyazov) meet Chernomyrdin
Davlat Usmon meets Taliban leadership in Kabul and relays a letter from Nuri
Rahmonov announces sending an envoy to Tehran for cease-fire talks with Nuri
Uzbek aid program for Dostam begins when Dostam and Rabbani were allies
Uzbek aid program for Dostam begins when Dostam and Rabbani were allies.
Dostam and Rabbani split.
Davlat Usmon met Taliban leadership in Kabul to discuss joint efforts against the Tajik Government and delivered Nuri's letter.
Rahmonov announced sending an envoy to Tehran for cease-fire talks with Nuri.
Niyazov refused Iranian request to transit military equipment to Dostam across Turkmen territory.
Niyazov-Yeltsin meeting scheduled in Moscow for the following week.
Kyrgyzstan moved Osh brigade troops and Russian border guards to the Kyrgyz-Tajik border.
Nazarbayev offered to mediate in Afghanistan and called for a UN Security Council meeting on Kabul.
Taliban captured Kabul unexpectedly.
Emergency CIS Summit in Almaty on Afghan crisis with Chernomyrdin and four Central Asian leaders; no agreement on reinforcing borders or arming Dostam and Masood.
Tajikistan and Russia bilaterally agreed to reinforce Tajik-Afghan border with additional Russian border troops.
Karimov at press conference called for increased support to Dostam; at Summit rejected Russian proposal for an anti-Taliban front.
Rahmonov announced sending envoy to Tehran to discuss cease-fire proposal with Nuri.
Uzbek aid program for Dostam began approximately in 1992 when Dostam and Rabbani were allies.
Dostam and Rabbani split at end of 1993.
A second echelon of CIS peacekeeping troops was reportedly set up along the Tajik-Afghan border.
Karimov stated that Uzbekistan would send forces into Afghanistan if the Uzbek and Tajik borders were violated.

key_claims: Central Asian states fear Taliban's capture of Kabul will destabilize their borders but have not agreed to a collective effort to arm its opponents.
Uzbekistan secretly supports Dostam with military and economic aid in exchange for keeping fighting from the Uzbek-Afghan border.
Karimov rejected a Russian-proposed anti-Taliban front fearing Iranian dominance, yet agreed to transit of Russian arms to Dostam.
Tajik Islamic opposition leader Davlat Usmon met Taliban leaders in Kabul, though there is little hard evidence of cooperation.
Turkmenistan stays neutral, supplies fuel to Taliban, and maintains good relations with Dostam.
Tajik and Central Asian officials claimed the US supports Taliban, echoing Russian allegations.
Kazakstan and Kyrgyzstan each have 500 troops in CIS Peacekeeping Forces in Tajikistan and would intervene if Taliban reached the borders.
